notes.blurb: The poor ring of an earth-built city: mud brick and rough stone under dark tile, crowded and low.
notes.construction: Mud-brick walls on a cobblestone footing with dark spruce posts and lintels; small openings, party walls, no gardens.
notes.ground: Packed mud lanes between the houses, no paving.
notes.roofs: Single-tier hipped roofs of dark tile, pitched one-in-one and hipped at both ends so a roof can run unbroken over a row of party-walled houses. The eave is straight and oversails one block: the narrowest overhang that still throws a shadow line (S202), because in a lane four blocks wide a wider one meets the roof opposite. **A design decision, not a source's claim**: the crowded ring's roof is the middle ring's roof with everything expensive taken off it -- one pitch instead of two, a straight eave instead of a turned-up one, one block of oversail instead of two, hipped ends instead of an irimoya. The taxonomy and the shadow-line rule are S200, S201 and S202; which end of it a poor ring gets is this voice's decision.
notes.signature: A sea of dark roofs on earth-coloured walls, reading from the air as one brown-grey belt against the green tile of the rings within.
